outcome: Help commercial insurers and brokers quote suitable risks faster by extracting submission data, highlighting gaps, and preparing explainable underwriting recommendations.
overview: Commercial underwriting submissions arrive as emails, spreadsheets, schedules, loss runs, surveys and PDFs — and underwriters spend much of their day re-keying and reconciling before judgement even begins. This solution classifies and extracts submission evidence, maps it to the insurer’s data schema, checks completeness, summarises exposures and loss history, retrieves approved guidelines with citations, and presents an explainable risk and pricing workbench. The underwriter retains full authority over risk selection, terms, exclusions and price. An 8–12-week proof of value focuses on one product and broker channel, targeting faster quote turnaround, more submissions per underwriter, consistent guideline use and structured portfolio data.

benefits.text: Reduce submission preparation time by a target 40–60%
benefits.limits: Basis: hypothesis. Target range to validate on the customer’s own submission mix during the PoV — not a guarantee

benefits.text: Increase submissions reviewed per underwriter by a target 20%
benefits.limits: Basis: hypothesis. Depends on document variability by product and broker channel

benefits.text: Record cited guideline evidence for every recommendation, improving referral consistency and portfolio data
benefits.source: Reference-design control (versioned guideline retrieval with citations); Redington BFSI catalogue
benefits.limits: Citation coverage is a platform control; guideline currency depends on the customer’s versioning discipline

residency: Deployable in-country on local AWS or Azure regions (e.g. UAE, KSA); a hybrid option keeps proprietary pricing models and sensitive submissions on customer-controlled infrastructure

notFor.situation: Underwriting guidelines and authority rules are out of date or unowned
notFor.why: The workbench retrieves and cites approved guidelines; retrieving stale rules would systematise error rather than judgement

notFor.situation: Submission volume is low and highly bespoke (large single-risk placements only)
notFor.why: Extraction and schema mapping pay back on repeatable document patterns; one-off bespoke placements keep the manual economics

notFor.situation: The insurer expects automated quote issuance without underwriter review
notFor.why: The design keeps risk selection, terms, exclusions and price with the underwriter; delegated-authority automation is a different, regulated proposition

scope:
Model: Joint delivery: accredited implementation partner leads, with Redington architecture and commercial governance; the customer owns underwriting authority, terms and pricing · Duration: 8–12 weeks PoV; 14–24 weeks to production
Delivery pod: Partner project and technical leads, vendor platform specialist; customer underwriting sponsor, product and rating owners, data owner, security approver, broker-operations lead and underwriters · Support model: Business-hours standard with an extended option; severity-based targets; partner first line with vendor escalation; optional managed intake
1) Discovery, schema and guideline design
2) Document benchmark
3) Workbench build and integration
4) Security and quality testing
5) Underwriter training and UAT
6) Controlled launch, stabilisation and handover
